title: §154-Listed BESS Suppliers — US Market-Access Risk
topic: US market-access, policy, and counterparty risk across the covered FY2024 NDAA §154(b)-listed battery makers

scope.rationale: The five covered names on the FY2024 NDAA §154(b) list — the statutory perimeter of the US policy fence; Gotion is listed but not covered by a dossier.

gaps: Gotion is §154(b)-listed but has no dossier — the statutory set is six, this report covers five.

Statutory and tax mechanics (MACR floors, tariff stack, safe-harbor dates) are summarized from internal policy research — the Industry Guidance China-policy module — not from dossier citations; every such passage is inside an analysis-flagged section.

EVE's reported addition to the DoD §1260H list (Jun 2026, per Reuters as recorded in the dossier's developments) has no citable source entry in the dossier — treated throughout as reported, not established.
No cross-company financial comparison is drawn: the normalized-KPI overlay is not used (Envision carries none), and segment-level US revenue is not comparably disclosed by any of the five.

bluf: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: The US policy fence does not threaten the five covered §154-listed makers' growth — all five keep compounding outside it — but it decides HOW each one can touch the US market: through safe-harbored and merchant projects, US assembly as a tariff lever, or divest-to-comply structures. We assess the sharpest differentiator inside the set is financing and litigation posture, with Hithium the acute counterparty case and CATL the counter-case.

keyJudgments.text: We assess the policy fence bifurcates the five's US business into structures rather than direct sales: for 2026+ construction starts, systems built on their cells forfeit the storage ITC under the prohibited-foreign-entity rules that imported the §154(b) list into the tax code, leaving safe-harbored 2025 projects and merchant/tax-indifferent buyers as the addressable direct lanes.

We assess financing posture is the sharpest company-specific divergence in the set. CATL raised HK$41B in the largest IPO of 2025; Hithium has now failed three listing attempts (the second HKEX prospectus lapsed 27 Apr 2026 with no re-filing observed) and carries a controlling-shareholder equity freeze plus ~10 pending CATL suits; EVE's H-share prospectus lapsed once and was re-filed amid a CSRC probe. Counterparty-risk premium concentrates on the unlisted names.

We assess the divest-to-comply structure — AESC's US cell plant passing to Fixx Energy, feeding Fluence's domestic-content line and a 10 GWh Prevalon deal — is the only lane currently putting listed-maker technology inside FEOC-clean US supply chains at scale. Ford's CATL license is the only other working template, and the collapse of Hithium's Reliance licensing deal shows how fragile the license lane is.

We assess US assembly is a tariff lever, not a tax fix: Hithium's Texas plant has shipped since Aug 2025 and shortens delivery while cutting the dutiable base to cell value, but a listed maker's US output remains PFE-made for ITC purposes. Its value accrues to the merchant lane only.

We assess the fence redirects rather than caps growth: BYD's 11.275 GWh Masdar award, Hithium's Australia/Saudi/Europe run, CATL's 27.1% H1 2026 global ESS share and European sodium partnerships, and a 2025 cell market that nearly doubled to 612 GWh all sit outside US jurisdiction. The competitive cost of the fence is US reference fleets and bankability records, not volume.

We assess that in the one code-driven US category still open to contest (AI data-center buffering), the listed names are not setting terms: Hithium's AIDC line showed no named customers in the months after launch, and Jupiter Power — its US anchor account — planted domestic sodium supplier Peak Energy on precisely the chemistry Hithium markets as its next act.

sections.title: The fence, briefly
ps: Four federal machines constrain the set, on four legal levers: tax (the prohibited-foreign-entity rules attached to the storage ITC, which incorporate the §154(b) roster by name [c:c19] [c:c18]), trade (the tariff stack on Chinese lithium-ion), defense procurement (the §154 DoD ban from Oct 1, 2027), and the domestic-content adder. The tax lever is decisive: a 2026-construction-start system on any of these five makers' cells fails the material-assistance cost floor and forfeits the entire ITC — a ~30%-of-capex swing. *(Assessment note: the cost-ratio arithmetic is summarized from internal policy research — the Industry Guidance China-policy module carries the mechanics with statutory citations; it is not re-derived from dossier sources here.)*

What the fence does not do is prohibit the sale. Safe-harbored 2025 construction starts keep their ITC, merchant and tax-indifferent buyers have no credit to lose, and none of the trade or tax levers touch the five's non-US business — which is where their 2025-26 growth actually happened [c:c1].

US soil does not cleanse the product: a listed maker's US-assembled output remains PFE-made for tax purposes [c:c19]. That is why Texas assembly functions as a tariff-and-logistics lever for the merchant lane [c:c5] while the only structure that has produced genuinely FEOC-clean US supply is ownership separation — the AESC/Fixx divestiture [c:c20].

sections.title: The counterparty files
ps: **Hithium** carries the set's acute file. The second HKEX prospectus lapsed on 27 Apr 2026 — the third failed listing attempt after the withdrawn A-share run and the lapsed March 2025 application — with no re-filing observed since [c:c2]. Chinese financial press reports ~10 pending CATL-initiated suits exceeding RMB 240M in claims and a controlling-shareholder equity freeze running to Feb 2029 [c:c3]. The lapsed prospectus itself is the primary public window into its financials [c:c4]. Against that: Top-2 2025 ESS cell shipments in a market that nearly doubled to 612 GWh [c:c1], the approved 2.8 GWh Trimount project anchoring its US fleet [c:c6], and a shipping Texas plant [c:c5].

**EVE Energy** is the swing file: the cycle turned violently in its favor — H1 2026 profit guided +95-110% [c:c17] — while its US-facing risk accumulated: the LG/Tulip patent action added an ITC Section 337 front [c:c15], the H-share prospectus lapsed and was re-filed amid a CSRC probe [c:c16], Powin's bankruptcy erased its largest US contracted position [c:c23], and its dossier records a reported addition to the DoD §1260H list (Jun 2026, per Reuters — reported, not established here).

**CATL** is the counter-case on financing — the HK$41B Hong Kong raise was the largest IPO of 2025 [c:c10] — and its US exposure is structurally different: technology reaches the US through Ford's license-built plant rather than through CATL-branded supply [c:c11]. **BYD** and **Envision** sit between: BYD's storage book is concentrated outside the US [c:c13] [c:c12], and Envision's US story is now the Fixx/AESC structure rather than its own brand [c:c20] [c:c21], with the Florence SC halt showing the cost side of the same policy stack [c:c22].

sections.title: The lanes that remain — as actually used
ps: **1 — Safe-harbored pipeline.** The primary direct lane through 2027. Jupiter's Trimount (2.8 GWh on Hithium units, EFSB-approved Feb 2026) is the working example [c:c6].

**2 — Merchant / tax-indifferent buyers.** Nothing prohibits the sale; the seller must beat FEOC-clean rivals net of their ITC. Texas assembly helps this lane on duty base and delivery speed [c:c5] — and only this lane.

**3 — Divest-to-comply.** The structural escape that is actually producing US volume: AESC's Smyrna plant under Fixx Energy ownership supplies Fluence's domestic-content line (~50% of its US project cells) [c:c21] and a 3-year, 10 GWh Prevalon deal [c:c20].

**4 — License.** Ford's CATL-license plant is producing [c:c11]; Hithium's Reliance licensing deal collapsed and took the partner's cell program with it [c:c24]. One working template, one cautionary tale — treat every license pitch as contingent.
**5 — Non-US markets.** Where the growth is: Masdar's 11.275 GWh award [c:c13], CATL's H1 2026 share gains [c:c9], BYD's 2025 crown [c:c12]. The US fence costs reference fleets, not volume.

guidanceOverlays.title: Who the levers actually bite
ps: Of the covered five on the §154(b) roster, **Hithium is the acute case**: captured by name and as a Chinese-organized company, with the thinnest balance sheet in the set — three failed listing attempts (the second HKEX prospectus lapsed 27 Apr 2026, no re-filing observed), a controlling-shareholder equity freeze to Feb 2029, and ~10 pending CATL suits. The tax lever's severity lands hardest where the financing cushion is thinnest.

**EVE** now carries a second statutory route per its dossier: a reported DoD §1260H addition (Jun 2026) — an independent SFE pathway on top of §154(b). **CATL and BYD** absorb the same levers on scale and non-US demand; **Envision** turned the defense lever's cost side into the set's only working FEOC-clean US lane by divesting AESC's Tennessee plant to Fixx Energy.

guidanceOverlays.title: The interaction map, live
ps: Every lane in this section has a named 2026 example among the covered five. Safe-harbored pipeline: Jupiter's Trimount — 2.8 GWh on Hithium 5.015 MWh units, EFSB-approved Feb 2026. Tariff engineering via US assembly: Hithium's Texas plant, shipping since Aug 2025 — duty on cell value, still PFE-made for tax. Compliant supply chain: AESC under Fixx ownership feeding Fluence's domestic-content line and a 10 GWh Prevalon deal. License: Ford/CATL producing; Hithium/Reliance collapsed.

The map's teaching point holds in practice: **no lane fixed the 2026+ ITC math for a listed maker's own brand** — the working structures either predate the fence (safe harbor), avoid the credit (merchant), or separate ownership (Fixx).

guidanceOverlays.title: Hithium's live file (Aug 2026)
ps: **Tailwinds an IE credits:** Top-2 2025 ESS cell shipments in a 612 GWh market; the approved Trimount 2.8 GWh anchor project; a shipping Texas assembly plant; grid-forming deliveries compounding in Australia/Saudi/Europe.

**Headwinds an IE flags:** the second HKEX prospectus lapsed 27 Apr 2026 — the third failed listing attempt, with no re-filing observed; a controlling-shareholder equity freeze running to Feb 2029; ~10 pending CATL suits exceeding RMB 240M; prospectus-disclosed margin compression; and the FEOC overlay on all 2026+ US ITC projects.

**Peer flags in the same set:** EVE's lapsed-and-refiled H-share prospectus amid a CSRC probe, its LG/Tulip ITC §337 action, and a reported §1260H addition. **The counter-case:** CATL's HK$41B raise — financing strength is the widest spread inside the §154 set.

guidanceOverlays.title: Where each listed maker actually sits
ps: **Hithium:** merchant + safe-harbored only — the Jupiter fleet (Trimount approved) and urban NYC projects; zero regulated self-build presence. **Envision/AESC:** the set's only entry into the regulated, domestic-content lane — via the Fixx divestiture supplying Fluence (~50% of its US project cells) and Prevalon (10 GWh). **CATL:** reaches the US through Ford's license-built plant, not its own brand. **BYD/EVE:** effectively non-US stories for regulated purposes; EVE's largest US contracted position died with Powin's Chapter 11.

Account note: Jupiter — Hithium's US anchor — signed Peak Energy for sodium (720 MWh + up to 4 GWh reserved), planting a domestic supplier inside the account on the chemistry Hithium markets as its next act. Defending that account on economics, delivery record, and augmentation terms is the highest-leverage US sales action in the Hithium file.

guidanceOverlays.title: Channel reality for the §154 set
ps: For the covered listed makers, only two of the five channels are live in the US: **ERCOT merchant** and the merchant-adjacent safe-harbored pipeline (Jupiter/Trimount is the flagship). The three regulated channels — storage RFPs, all-source RFPs, and self-build — are effectively fenced for their branded product on prudence + FEOC grounds; the only listed-maker technology inside those channels arrives through the AESC/Fixx domestic-content structure.

The ride-through buffering channel is nominally open (no ITC at stake for many campus buyers) but contested: Hithium's AIDC line launched without named customers while the FEOC-clean AI-UPS category leader set the US terms. Qualify hard before spending pipeline time there.
